chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Salim al-Ji'abi reported to me, he said: Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hasani narrated to us, he said: al-Fadl ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: my father narrated to me, from my grandfather, from his father, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil ibn Abi Talib, who said: I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon them both) say:

A nerve of a believer does not twitch nor does he suffer a headache except because of his sin, and that which Allah forgives is far more. And whenever he saw a sick person who had recovered, he would say: May the purification from sins bring you joy! Now start your deeds anew.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about illness and sin?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) taught that every affliction a believer experiences, even a minor twitch or headache, occurs as a consequence of sin, yet God's forgiveness far exceeds what He holds accountable. The Imam, who lived in Medina in the late first century AH, used to congratulate those recovering from illness, viewing recovery as purification from sins and an opportunity to begin good deeds afresh.
